rationale: Repair attempt for trial-3c2ed50501 at the same whole-decode-step boundary (group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f, decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM module call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, 31 invocations per run). The previous feedback records one concrete failure: per-step output.logits exceeded the 0.02 tolerance on both continuous quality steps (27.6% of 4,861,952 elements, max abs error 1.65625 at step index 3, the first graph-produced step; eager steps 0-2 and coverage counting were fine), so the hand-written composite mis-tracked value dynamics inside the captured region rather than graph replay or the boundary being wrong. This candidate therefore never re-implements decode math: it captures the UNCHANGED parent forward itself. The replacement builds a preallocated transformers 5.16.1 StaticCache window (prompt_tokens+new_tokens+8 = 296 slots), whose per-layer cumulative_length is a device scalar updated in-place (cache_utils.py:415,442,476); StaticLayer.update derives cache_position on device via arange+cumulative_length and writes in-place with index_copy_ (cache_utils.py:474-481), Qwen3Model.forward derives position_ids from the cache on device (modeling_qwen3.py:386-389) and create_causal_mask materializes the bool mask from the device query offset with static kv_length=max_cache_len (masking_utils.py:829-833,952-954), so the whole step is value-dynamic and capture-compatible with no rewritten kernels. Each invocation re-seeds the window from that invocation's own prefill DynamicCache (per-layer slice copies plus device position reset), then every step copies the incoming token into the static input buffer and runs: two eager parent-on-static steps, then one capture (side-stream warmups, torch.cuda.graph capture_error_mode='thread_local'), verified by torch.equal of the replayed logits against the eager parent output on identical inputs before the graph is ever trusted, then pure replay for all remaining steps of all invocations. Because the replayed kernels are the parent's own on live buffers, the only numerical delta versus the DynamicCache reference is masked padded-window SDPA (repeat_kv + bool mask over 296 slots) versus unmasked GQA flash over the exact length; a CPU structural check with the measured worker's python (tiny random Qwen3, worker-environment.json executable, no GPU launches) reproduced exact greedy-token equality and max logit abs error 1.2e-7 for the static versus dynamic parent across a 5-step decode, and bitwise-identical output on a second re-seeded invocation. Measured motivation (unchanged from selection): decode is 96.6% of the end-to-end window (704.4 of 728.8ms, project.json original_baseline) and host-launch-bound - 66,441 kernels at 5.9us mean in the nsys diagnostic, execution_timeline shows 386.8ms device-active union against 1,159.6ms of inter-kernel gaps, and nested decode CUDA time is 373.8ms against 704.4ms decode wall - so removing per-step host dispatch is expected to move decode toward the ~12.1ms/step device floor (~370-420ms window, ~70-80 tok/s); this expectation is to be confirmed by the framework's independent measurement, not claimed as observed. Exactly 32 tokens are generated, prefill/argmax/cat/timing boundaries and thresholds are untouched, and any signature mismatch, setup failure, capacity problem, capture/verify failure or runtime error falls back to the unchanged parent on the original arguments with the device cache positions rewound so the returned cache object stays consistent. The 23,225 eliminated descendant calls (Qwen3Model, 36 decoder layers, attention/MLP/norm modules, aten::linear, sdpa, cat and elementwise decode sites) run inside the parent forward during the eager/capture steps and are reproduced by graph replay otherwise; their consumers remain valid because the replacement returns the parent's own result structure (CausalLMOutputWithPast with cloned per-step logits and the advanced cache) and the adapter-level shared calls (argmax, generated-token cat, discovery hooks) keep executing.

setup_work.build_time: CPU-only: resolve the module tree and config (36 layers, 32 q heads, 8 kv heads, head_dim 128, hidden 2560, bf16, all layers full_attention so StaticLayer applies), probe the submodules the decode path touches, and plan the static capacity (prompt_tokens+new_tokens+8=296). No GPU work, no parameter transforms, nothing cached at build; build returns only the single replacement callable.
setup_work.first_invocation: Lazily inside the first measured-lifecycle invocation (a warmup/quality execution precedes the timed repeats): early-initialize the StaticCache (36 layers x 2 tensors [1,8,296,128] bf16, ~43.7MB, plus per-layer device cumulative_length scalars moved to the GPU and mark_static_address'd), allocate the [1,1] int64 static input buffer; the first decode step of EVERY invocation copies 36x2 KV slices from that invocation's prefill DynamicCache into the window and resets the device positions. Capture happens once, at decode step 2 of the first invocation: 2 side-stream warmup executions + capture + one verified replay (torch.equal against the eager parent output), i.e. about three extra step executions once, outside the timed repeats. Every later step is one d2d token copy + graph.replay() + logits clone.
setup_work.memory_scope: Setup allocation is explicit: ~43.7MB bf16 static KV window plus small buffers, allocated during the first invocation and retained for the process lifetime; the captured CUDA graph retains a private memory pool holding the step's intermediates (mask, repeat_kv-expanded keys/values, activations, logits), which increases framework.lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes and keeps warm-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes higher than a pure replay would suggest. Baseline peak_allocated is 8.17GB on the 24GB RTX 4090 (project.json), so headroom is ample; the retained pool is reported as setup/retained memory, not described as a general physical-memory saving, and no driver-external allocation is measured by these counters.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: Single-process single-GPU; no collectives, streams shared with the harness, or process groups. The static window, input buffer and graph persist across invocations (measurement_lifetime=invocation); per-invocation state is only the re-seeded window contents, a host mirror of the write position kept in lockstep with the device cumulative_length scalars, and the continuing-call identity check on the returned cache object. On any runtime failure the device positions are rewound to the host mirror before falling back to the parent, so the cache object previously returned to the adapter stays consistent.

quality_risks: Static-path numerics differ microscopically from the DynamicCache reference: the materialized bool mask plus repeat_kv (sdpa GQA is skipped when a mask is present) over the padded 296-slot window versus unmasked GQA flash over the exact length. The fp32 CPU sanity check showed max abs error 1.2e-7 and exact greedy equality, but bf16 on the leased GPU could still show ~1-2 ulp differences; these are far below atol/rtol 0.02, yet an argmax near-tie between top-2 logits could in principle flip one greedy token. The torch.equal verify only proves graph fidelity to the eager static parent, not to the reference path.

cuBLAS/SDPA kernel selection can depend on pointer alignment; if the captured graph's pool addresses select different kernels than the eager warmup allocations, the torch.equal verification fails and the candidate permanently stays on the eager static path (correct results, no graph speedup).

CUDA graph capture itself may fail in the worker (cuBLAS workspaces, allocator behavior, any hidden host sync in library code); capture runs with capture_error_mode='thread_local' and every capture exception is caught, falling back to eager static-parent steps that still pass quality but regain only the removed DynamicCache churn, not the dispatch gap.

The mask/position derivation must remain fully device-side under capture; any host-side read of the cumulative_length scalars inside the parent path would abort capture (caught -> fallback) rather than silently corrupt, based on the inspected 5.16.1 source, but only worker execution proves it.

Per-step host work remains (signature guards, token copy, replay submission, logits clone, output object construction); if replay submission plus clone approached the ~12ms device step time the throughput gain would shrink - a performance risk, not a correctness risk.
Memory accounting changes: retained graph pool and static window raise lifecycle reserved/allocated counters as documented in setup_work; peak_allocated_bytes per run includes the retained window.
